chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAwwāḍ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Ghusl suffices in place of wudu (ablution); and what wudu (ablution) is purer than ghusl?

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام, the narrator from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.أَطْهَرُ: purer, more purifying in ritual terms
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl (ritual bath), the act said here to suffice for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يُجْزِئُ: is sufficient, fulfills the required obligation

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl suffice in place of wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that ghusl is sufficient in place of wudu (ablution). It expresses the legal sufficiency of ghusl for ritual purity and emphasizes its greater purifying quality.
